previous_last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU clarified the lambda-protection minimum and restore load thresholds so their guidance follows the selected lambda load source instead of always showing percent. The two merge commits integrate that change and add no further user-facing behavior.

decisions.rationale: The lambda-protection minimum and restore load fields no longer display a fixed percent unit. Their help text now states that thresholds use the selected lambda load source units: MAP or effective MAP in kPa, throttle, pedal or cylinder filling in percent, and fuel-model units for Model default. No tune layout or value range changed, so no retune or migration is required; existing numeric thresholds keep their stored values but must be read in the units of the currently selected Threshold load source.

last_sync.summary: Capoworks ECU now keeps STEP/DIR idle stepper drivers enabled between steps, waits a fixed 2 ms after enabling before the first STEP edge, and releases the driver after five seconds without movement or when main-relay power or battery voltage is unavailable. The idle hardware page documents the new timing and power-loss behavior.

decisions.rationale: Capoworks ECU changes STEP/DIR idle stepper behavior. The driver enable output now stays asserted between steps instead of being released after every pulse, a fixed 2 ms settle delay follows each enable before the first STEP edge, and the driver is released after five seconds without movement. The driver is also released, and no step is taken, when main-relay power is off or battery voltage is below the minimum stepper voltage, including during the 2 ms enable delay. No tune fields or calibration layout change, so no tune migration is needed. Verify the enable polarity and wiring for the installed board, and confirm the minimum stepper voltage setting matches the hardware before relying on the power-loss release.
